summary: The US votes Tuesday while Iran waits on Washington's answer, Ukraine's local truce ends, Israel's leaders are urged to compromise, and North Korea is blamed for a record crypto theft.

topics.heading: Iran sends its two-day Hormuz plan to Washington through Qatar
topics.summary: Iran's negotiators left Doha after three days of talks with Qatari mediators, and Tehran says its plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is now with the US. President Trump says the war will end soon "one way or the other", and strikes after Tuesday's US vote remain possible.[^1][^3]

lead.title: Iranian negotiators depart Doha, but talks with Qatar not derailed, says official

alsoReported.title: Mediators continue US-Iran negotiations amid war rhetoric: What we know
Trump, Rubio say more Iran strikes are still on the table, but not likely before midterms

article: Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday after three days of talks with Qatar's mediators. An Iranian official told Reuters the departure did not mean the talks had run into trouble, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussion of a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is continuing[^1]. On Monday, Tehran said the proposal has been passed to the US through Qatar and that the next move is Washington's; if the US accepts, Iran says, "security will be restored" in the strait and wider negotiations could start[^3].

The plan comes with conditions. According to Al Jazeera, Iran wants recent US sanctions lifted, oil waivers restored, fewer US forces in the region, recognition of shipping routes set by Iran and Oman, and an end to fighting on all fronts, including Israeli attacks in Lebanon[^2]. AP reports that an earlier Iranian offer to reopen the strait within a week was rejected by the US[^4]. Araghchi says Iran has no plan to meet US officials directly[^4].

Both sides are mixing talks with threats. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Trump "hasn't made a decision" on new strikes and prefers diplomacy[^4]. Trump calls the talks "going fine" but "not very reliable", and on Monday said the war will end "very soon" with either a deal or "the hammer"[^2][^3]. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered a wider list of targets for any response, and security official Mohsen Rezaei spoke of "new weaponry"[^2].

Why it matters: the strait carries a large share of the world's oil, and it has been mostly shut for months. US oil prices closed above $104 a barrel on Friday[^24]. That cost reaches petrol stations and grocery bills far from the Gulf, including in Canada.

What comes next depends on Washington. Trump has said there will be no new attacks before Tuesday's election, but has not ruled them out afterwards[^1]. My read: the next few days will show whether the US treats Iran's plan as a starting point or a stalling tactic.
topics.differences: Iran says it has made its offer and the next step is Washington's[^3]. Trump calls Iran's negotiators unreliable and keeps strikes on the table, while Rubio says no decision has been made[^2][^4]. Reports that Gulf states were told to prepare for a short conflict after the vote come from unnamed sources and are not confirmed[^2].

topics.heading: Over 53 million Americans vote early as the US midterms arrive on Tuesday
topics.summary: More than 53 million ballots were cast before Tuesday's US midterm elections, well ahead of 2022. Polls give Democrats a clear national lead, and several Senate races in Republican-leaning states look close.[^5][^7]

lead.title: More than 50 million votes cast in US midterm elections: What does it mean?

alsoReported.title: Donald Trump makes final midterm campaign push
Hottest 2026 Midterm Races: Democrats Lead Almost All Major Senate Contests

article: On Tuesday, Americans elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 senators. Republicans now hold narrow majorities in both chambers[^6]. Midterms fall halfway through a president's term and often go against the president's party.

Turnout before election day has been unusually high. By Sunday, more than 53 million people had voted early, in person or by mail, compared with about 46 million in 2022, according to a University of Florida count cited by Al Jazeera[^5]. About 11 million registered Democrats had voted, against about 8 million registered Republicans, though that does not show how anyone voted[^5]. Early voting rose by more than 80% in South Carolina and by about a third in Michigan and Kansas[^5].

Polls lean toward Democrats. The Silver Bulletin average of the national House vote shows Democrats at about 51% and Republicans at about 42%[^7]. YouGov polls show Democrats narrowly ahead in Senate races in Texas and Maine, and a tie in Nebraska between Republican Pete Ricketts and independent Dan Osborn[^7]. Polls can miss, especially in close races, so these are signals, not results.
Al Jazeera links Republican weakness to the cost of living, tariffs and the unpopular Iran war[^5]. Trump held rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday and says he will "surprise a lot of people"[^6].

Why it matters: if Democrats win the House or Senate, they could block parts of Trump's agenda for his last two years and open investigations[^6]. For Canada, the result could shape the trade dispute and tariffs. Close races may take days to count, so control of the Senate may not be clear on Tuesday night.

topics.heading: Oleshky truce ends as Russian drone strikes leave Ukrainian homes without power
topics.summary: A rare local ceasefire that let civilians leave occupied Oleshky ended on Nov 1. Ukraine says both sides kept the deal, but also that Russia used the pause to resupply, while Russian drones again hit Ukraine's power grid.[^11][^9][^10]

lead.title: Civilians in Kherson prepare for return of war as localised ceasefire ends

alsoReported.title: Melania Trump hails Oleshky evacuation as success, but civilians remain trapped and Russia reinforces positions
Russian attacks kill 1, injure 47 over past day, leaving hundreds of thousands without electricity

article: For five days, guns were meant to fall silent around Oleshky, a town in Ukraine's Kherson region that Russia has occupied since 2022. The truce, mediated by the Vatican with help from US First Lady Melania Trump, let aid in and civilians out; it ended on Nov 1[^11]. Evacuees travelled by a long route through Russia and Belarus to reach Ukrainian-held land[^8].

How many left is unclear. Melania Trump says nearly 800 were evacuated, while AP reports that about 2,000 civilians had been in the town and that exact numbers were withheld to protect those who stayed[^9][^8]. Some who wanted to leave, including bedridden people, are still there, according to a source quoted by hromadske[^9].

Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, says both sides kept their commitments and is exploring more humanitarian deals with his Russian counterpart[^11]. At the same time, Ukraine's General Staff says Russian troops used the pause to rotate, dig in and resupply[^9]. Both statements can be true: a truce can serve civilians and armies at once.

Elsewhere the war went on. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched 433 drones overnight into Nov 1 and that 371 were shot down; regional officials reported one person killed and at least 47 injured, and President Zelensky says hundreds of thousands of families lost power[^10]. Ukraine says it hit military sites in Russia's Rostov region, and Russian media reported a fire at the Kstovo oil refinery[^8].

What next: Trump said Oleshky could be "the starting point for lasting peace"[^11]. My read: small humanitarian deals have happened before without leading to wider talks, and winter strikes on energy are likely to continue.
topics.differences: Ukraine's ombudsman says both sides kept the truce's terms, while Ukraine's military says Russia used it to reinforce[^11][^9]. Evacuee numbers differ: Melania Trump says nearly 800; AP says exact numbers were withheld[^9][^8].

topics.heading: Herzog urges Israel's leaders to compromise as Gaza strikes kill eight
topics.summary: With no bloc holding a majority after Israel's Oct 27 election, President Herzog told leaders to "stop climbing trees" and avoid another vote. In Gaza, hospitals say Israeli strikes killed eight people on Sunday, testing a fragile truce.[^12][^14]

lead.title: 'Stop climbing trees': Herzog offers party leaders ladders down, signals push for unity government

alsoReported.title: Joint List, Ra'am to back Gadi Eisenkot for premiership as Isaac Herzog opens negotiations
Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say

article: Israel's Oct 27 election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc with 53 of 120 seats, the Jewish-led opposition parties with 48 and the Arab-led parties with a record 19[^12]. A government needs 61. The opposition adds up to 67, but several of its parties refuse to govern with the Arab-led factions[^12].

On Sunday President Isaac Herzog told party leaders to "stop climbing trees, and face reality", and offered them "ladders" to climb down from earlier promises; reporters read this as a push toward a unity government[^12]. The Arab-led Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend former army chief Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister[^13]. Likud is split: one member says Netanyahu wants a unity government, while the party whip rejects sharing the top job in rotation[^12].

In Gaza, hospitals say Israeli strikes killed at least eight people on Sunday, including five police officers in al-Mawasi and a four-year-old boy in Gaza City[^14][^15]. Israel's military says it targeted militants and gave no evidence; Hamas called the strikes a war crime[^15]. Gaza's Health Ministry says about 1,580 people have been killed since the ceasefire began in October 2025[^14].

Why it matters: the next phase of the US-backed Gaza plan, including disarmament and reconstruction, is stalled, and it is waiting in part for a new Israeli government[^14]. Who governs Israel will shape what happens next in Gaza.
What next: Herzog receives official results and starts meeting parties on Nov 4, and the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10[^12]. My read: talks could run for weeks, and another election is possible.
topics.differences: Israel's military says Sunday's strikes hit militants; Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry says police officers were killed and calls it a massacre[^14][^15]. Gaza's death toll since the truce is given as about 1,580 by the Health Ministry via the BBC, and as over 1,500 by Al Jazeera[^14][^15].

topics.heading: FBI blames North Korea for a $6.3-billion theft from crypto exchange Binance
topics.summary: Hackers took about $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest crypto exchange, in the biggest crypto theft on record. The FBI says a North Korean group did it; Binance says it covered losses from its own funds and reopened withdrawals.[^16][^17]

lead.title: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history: What we know

alsoReported.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after more than $6 bn stolen in hack; FBI says North Korea behind

article: Late on Oct 29, attackers drained about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes[^16]. That is about four times the previous record, the roughly $1.5-billion theft from the exchange Bybit in 2025[^16][^17].

The FBI says the hack was carried out by TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-linked group connected to the Lazarus Group, and that it has watched the stolen money being converted into Ether[^17]. North Korea routinely denies hacking[^16]. Binance has said its own investigation has not yet named anyone[^16].

About $3 billion has been frozen, more than $2.3 billion of it by Tether and Circle, two companies that issue "stablecoins" (crypto tokens tied to the US dollar)[^16]. Binance says it set aside more than $6.34 billion of its own money and has replaced about 90% of the stolen tokens; it planned to reopen withdrawals on Sunday[^17]. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low after the news[^16].

Why it matters: researchers have long said crypto theft helps fund North Korea's weapons programs, which the UN bans. A crypto investigator quoted by Al Jazeera calls this "a global security issue, not just a crypto theft"[^16]. It also shows that even the biggest platforms can be emptied in minutes.

What next: investigators will try to trace and freeze more of the money, and the FBI is asking firms to block the addresses used to launder it[^17]. My read: expect renewed pressure on governments to regulate exchanges more like banks.
topics.differences: The FBI names a North Korean group; Binance says its own investigation has not attributed the attack, and North Korea routinely denies such accusations[^16][^17].

topics.heading: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 5,000 deaths, the second-deadliest on record
topics.summary: Congo's Health Ministry reports 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed Ebola cases. The strain has no approved vaccine, and health agencies say most new cases appear outside known contact chains.[^18][^19]

lead.title: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts

alsoReported.title: Death toll from Ebola outbreak in DR Congo surpasses 5,000

article: On Saturday, the Democratic Republic of Congo's Health Ministry reported 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed Ebola cases since the outbreak was declared in mid-May, meaning nearly half of those infected have died[^18][^19]. Only the 2014-16 outbreak in West Africa, with about 11,000 deaths, was deadlier[^18].

This outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment[^18]. It has reached 8 of Congo's 26 provinces, centred on Ituri and North Kivu in the east, and cases have been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and, earlier, Uganda[^18].

The hardest part is tracking it. Africa CDC says about 80% of new cases are appearing outside the lists of known contacts that health workers follow[^18]. Congo's health authorities say only about 12% of confirmed cases came from known contacts[^19]. When cases come from unknown sources, the virus is spreading in ways responders cannot see.
The response is also hampered by conflict in eastern Congo, attacks on clinics and strikes by unpaid health workers, AP reports[^18]. A WHO official called the toll "a very tragic milestone"[^18].

Why it matters: Ebola outbreaks are usually contained in one region. This one is the most widespread in Africa so far, and further spread across borders is the main fear[^18]. What next: health agencies are asking for more money and staff for testing and contact tracing; no new dates have been set.

topics.heading: Bulgaria elects Iliana Yotova, a critic of military aid to Ukraine, as president
topics.summary: Acting president Iliana Yotova won Bulgaria's presidential runoff with about 58% of the vote on a turnout near 27%. She favours a negotiated peace in Ukraine and better ties with Russia while keeping Bulgaria in the EU and NATO.[^21][^20]

lead.title: Initial results suggest Yotova wins runoff to become Bulgaria's first elected female president

alsoReported.title: Initial results show Bulgaria's acting president Yotova wins runoff election

article: Iliana Yotova won Sunday's runoff with 57.58% of the vote against Andrey Gyurov's 39.46%, with almost all polling stations counted[^21]. Turnout was about 27%, low even for Bulgaria[^21]. Gyurov conceded[^20]. Yotova becomes the country's first elected female president, and her five-year term starts on Jan 22, 2027[^21][^20].

Yotova, 62, has been acting president since January, when Rumen Radev resigned to run for parliament; Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party now holds 131 of 240 seats[^20]. She opposes sending weapons to Ukraine and favours a negotiated peace and better relations with Russia, while saying Bulgaria stays on its European path[^20][^22]. She said voters chose "dialogue, rather than division"[^21].

Bulgaria is a small EU and NATO member on the Black Sea, but its president speaks for it abroad and commands the armed forces. Its result adds to a group of European governments, including Hungary and Slovakia, that are more sceptical of military help for Ukraine.

Why it matters: EU decisions on Ukraine, such as sanctions on Russia, often need every member to agree. My read: one more sceptical voice makes those decisions slower, though Bulgaria's main policies are set by its government, not its president. Observers also warn that with the president and parliamentary majority on the same side, checks on power may weaken[^20].

question.text: Binance says it covered its customers' $6.3 billion loss with its own money. If big platforms always repay victims after a hack, how might that change the choices made by hackers, customers and the companies themselves?
